Sentinel settings

The configuration section of Sentinel — detection, baseline, CVE intelligence, border corroboration, blocklist feed, AI narrative and the response kill switch — shown beside the pipeline, the live scoring weights and ten runnable demonstrations.

What is it?#

Settings → Sentinel → Settings is where Sentinel, SATOM's security-correlation pipeline, is configured. The pane explains what it configures before the form: the pipeline stage by stage, the score bands and live weight table, and ten scenarios you can run against the real engine. Defaults make a fresh installation observant but inert: detection on, actions off, no traffic to any third party. Using Sentinel (incidents, context, response policy, blocklist) is described in Sentinel.

What does it do?#

The section has four parts:

  1. What Sentinel does, stage by stage — Collect → Normalize + dedup → Route → Correlate → Score → Policy gates → Respond / propose, each with the settings that govern it. The sweep runs every 3 minutes.
  2. The score, and what each band permits — the bands observe, investigate, recommend and semi-auto, and the live tables Adds points / Subtracts points read from the scorer.
  3. See it happen — ten scenarios against the live engine — each card runs synthetic evidence through the real scorer, bands and policy gates (simulation — nothing is written, no device is touched). The gate audit reads this installation's kill switch, policies and hourly budget.
  4. Sentinel — security correlation — the settings form, grouped by concern, with the response kill switch last; plus Extra configuration this module needs (topology map, hypervisor targets, collection targets, scheduled actions, local model host, CVE mirror content).

A health strip at the top shows Pipeline, Response engine (ARMED or disarmed — proposals only), Baseline usable, CVE mirror, Action transports verified and AI narrative. Every control and heading carries a ? with its explanation.

The other Sentinel entries in the menu belong to the Sentinel article: Context, Response policy, Border blocklist, Architecture and Incidents console.

Requirements#

  • The scheduled actions sentinel_sweep (every 3 minutes), sentinel_baseline (nightly) and sentinel_vuln_sync (daily) — see Scheduled actions.
  • For VM and host layers: a topology map (Sentinel → Context) and hypervisor targets. For HTTP and infra metrics: the collectors on Metrics.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Saving (POST /settings/sentinel) requires users.manage (Administrator), the same key that shows the pane inside the Admin Console. The standalone page /settings/sentinel and the demonstrations require the legacy view permission, which any granular view key grants (for example protection.view or monitoring.view; every system profile has it): holders can view the values (secrets are masked) and run the scenarios, but only administrators can change them, including Response engine armed — anyone else gets 403 Forbidden on save. A user with no view key is refused the page.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: saving Sentinel settings requires users.manage (before, an operator could save them, arming included, through the standalone page), the standalone page and its demonstrations require a view permission, and the AI model endpoint ships empty.

How to use#

  1. Open Settings → Sentinel → Settings (or /settings/sentinel).
  2. Read the health strip; click a scenario card to see how the live engine would score and gate it.
  3. Change values in the form. Each field shows its storage key (sentinel.<key>) and a ?.
  4. Click Save Sentinel settings. Flashes: - "Sentinel settings saved: N changed." or "Sentinel settings unchanged." - "Clamped to their allowed range: key -> value, …" when a number was out of range. - "These never-block entries are not valid CIDRs and protect nothing: …" for bad never-block lines.
  5. The page returns to where you saved (the pane or the standalone page).
  1. 1Observedefaults: detection on, response disarmed
  2. 2Tunewindows, baseline, severity floor; watch incidents
  3. 3Contexttrusted sources and maintenance windows (Sentinel → Context)
  4. 4Policyper-action response policy (Sentinel → Response policy)
  5. 5ArmResponse engine armed — last, and only after the above

Configuration#

Detection & correlation#

Field Description Required Example
Sentinel enabled Master switch. Off = the sweep returns immediately; collected data is untouched. Default: on. No on
Attack-log rows per device per sweep Upper bound per appliance per sweep. Default: 200; range 10–2000. No 200
Correlation window — before T0 (seconds) Default: 60; range 10–3600. No 60
Correlation window — after T0 (seconds) Default: 300; range 30–7200. No 300
Incident absorption window (minutes) How long an open incident absorbs matching events (same device + source + attack family). Default: 15; range 1–240. No 15
Minimum severity that may open an incident info, low, medium, high, critical. Default: low. No low

Behavioural baseline#

Field Description Required Example
Baseline learning window (days) How far back the nightly recompute reads. Default: 21; range 3–396. No 21
Deviation threshold (robust z, k x MAD) Anomalous when |value − median| / MAD exceeds this. Default: 6.0; range 1.0–50.0. No 6.0
Minimum samples before a bucket may fire Below this a bucket stays learning. Default: 12; range 3–500. No 12

Vulnerability intelligence#

Field Description Required Example
Enrich incidents from the local CVE mirror Reads the local mirror only; never contacts a third party. Default: on. No on
Allow the scheduled mirror sync to reach the internet Separate, deliberately off. Default: off. No off
Mirror source vulners, nvd, manual. Default: vulners. No vulners
Vulners API key Secret; blank keeps the stored value. Default: —. No —
Mirror is 'stale' after (days) Default: 7; range 1–90. No 7

Border corroboration#

Field Description Required Example
Border corroboration enabled Ask the FortiAnalyzer whether the border logged the source. Inert until an appliance is mapped in Sentinel → Context → Border map. Default: on. No on
Require border corroboration before listing an address An address the border never logged may not enter a border blocklist. Default: on. No on
Distinct border destinations that count as scanning Default: 10; range 2–1000. No 10
Border log rows per lookup Default: 200; range 10–2000. No 200
Border lookup timeout (seconds) Default: 20.0; range 5.0–120.0. No 20.0
Extra minutes searched either side of the window Absorbs clock skew. Default: 2; range 0–120. No 2
Collector clock offset from UTC (minutes) Minutes to add to UTC to get the FortiAnalyzer's wall clock. Default: 0; range −900–900. No 0

Border blocklist feed#

Field Description Required Example
Publish the border blocklist feed Serves /sentinel/feed/<token>/blocklist.txt; off = 404, entries still recorded. Default: off. No off
Feed token Secret; the whole authentication of the feed URL. Default: —. No —
Default entry TTL (hours) Hard ceiling 720 h regardless. Default: 24; range 1–720. No 24
Maximum live entries At the ceiling new entries are refused, never evicted. Default: 500; range 1–10000. No 500
Consider a fetched copy stale after (minutes) Default: 30; range 1–1440. No 30
Audit mirror repository (git URL) A separate repository — never SATOM's own source repository. Default: empty. No —
Mirror branch Default: main. No main
Mirror push credential Secret. Default: —. No —
Mirror automatically on every publish Off = mirror only on demand. Default: off. No off

AI reasoning#

Field Description Required Example
AI narrative on incidents The model writes an explanation; it cannot change a score or reach a device. Default: off. No off
Local model endpoint (Ollama / OpenAI-compatible) Base URL of your model host; the narrative call is a POST to <url>/api/chat. Must be an http:// or https:// URL; any other scheme (for example file://) is refused when the call is made. Empty keeps AI reasoning off even when AI narrative on incidents is on. Default: empty. No http://localhost:11434
Model name Default: qwen3:32b. No qwen3:32b
Model timeout (seconds) Default: 90; range 5–600. No 90
Only reason about incidents scoring at least Default: 40; range 0–100. No 40

Response & safety#

Field Description Required Example
Response engine armed GLOBAL KILL SWITCH. Off = Sentinel may propose actions and may not execute any, whatever the per-action policy says. Default: off. No off
Circuit breaker — max actions per hour Fleet-wide ceiling across all action types. Default: 6; range 1–100. No 6
Wait before judging effectiveness (minutes) Default: 5; range 1–120. No 5
Device-side block period (seconds) Written onto the IP list as a block period so the appliance lifts the block itself. Default: 600; range 30–3600. No 600
Hardened web protection profiles (one per line) The only profiles raise_protection may move a policy onto. Empty = that action never runs. Default: empty. No —
Never-block networks (one CIDR per line) Sources inside these are never blocked. Default: {ip}/8, {ip}/12, {ip}/16, 127.0.0.0/8. No {ip}/8, {ip}/12, {ip}/16, 127.0.0.0/8

Numbers outside their range are clamped on save; a blank number field keeps the default; a blank secret keeps the stored value.

Example#

🧪Example — Try before you arm

Leave Response engine armed off. Run the scenario cards: each shows the score, band, the factors that produced it and the gate audit against your live settings — typically Refused: … because the engine is disarmed. Once incidents look right for a week, define the response policy, then arm.

Result#

  • Values are stored in app_settings under sentinel.<key>; the audit entry sentinel.settings lists the changed keys (or no change).
  • The next sweep uses the new values.

Troubleshooting#

"These never-block entries are not valid CIDRs and protect nothing: …"#

Possible causes — a typo in Never-block networks. Unparseable lines are skipped (the rest still apply) and, for the border blocklist, an unreadable protection list refuses every listing.

Solution — fix or remove the listed lines and save.

"Clamped to their allowed range: …"#

Solution — none needed; the stored value is the clamped one shown. Choose a value inside the range if the clamp is not what you meant.

Pipeline shows "never run"#

Possible causes — the sentinel_sweep scheduled action does not exist or is disabled.

Solution — check Scheduled actions.

"The demo endpoint did not answer"#

Possible causes — the Sentinel module failed to load, your session expired, or your profile holds no view permission (the demonstrations are refused without one).

Solution — reload the page; check the application log.

"<address> NOT listed: …" when adding to the border blocklist#

Possible causes — with Require border corroboration before listing an address on (the default), an address enters the border blocklist only if the border lookup completed and found the address. Zero rows is not treated as an answer: a wrong ADOM or device in the border map, a collector on a different clock and a source the border genuinely never saw all return nothing. The refusal names which case it was: - border corroboration is required but disabled — nothing can be confirmed - no edge map for this appliance, so the address cannot be confirmed as a real border peer - border lookup failed: … - border was not consulted (or the reason the lookup did not run) - the border never logged this address as a source — …

Solution 1. For the first four, fix the cause: enable Border corroboration enabled, map the appliance in Sentinel → Context → Border map, or correct the FortiAnalyzer scope, its reachability or Collector clock offset from UTC (minutes). 2. If the border really never saw the address, do not list it — see below. To list it anyway on an incident, tick Accept the risk if the border did not confirm it and give a Reason; an override without a reason is refused, and the reason is recorded on the entry.

Verification — the incident's border verdict shows the entries the border logged, and the listing succeeds.

AI narrative stays empty#

Possible causes — AI narrative on incidents is off, Local model endpoint is empty or unreachable, or the incident scored below Only reason about incidents scoring at least.

Solution — set a reachable model endpoint; incidents keep their score and evidence either way.

The incident says "The model did not answer: ValueError: ai_url must be an http(s) URL"#

Possible causes — Local model endpoint uses a scheme other than http or https. The value is saved as typed and refused each time SATOM calls the model.

Solution — enter the endpoint as http://<host>:11434 (or https://…) and save.

Advanced#

Advanced Implementation notes
  • The form is generated from the same catalog the code reads its values through, so a setting cannot appear in the form without being used.
  • A switch posts a hidden <key>__present marker so that turning it off is saved.
  • If the Sentinel module cannot be imported, the section renders empty instead of breaking the whole Settings page.
  • Band thresholds come from the incident model: observe below 40, recommend from 70, semi-auto from 85.
Advanced Why the border has to corroborate

The source address in a FortiWeb attack log depends on the policy: when it reads X-Forwarded-For the log carries the true client, which the firewall in front never saw as a peer; when it does not, the log carries whatever opened the connection — behind a CDN, the CDN itself. Both look like ordinary addresses and nothing in the log tells them apart. The border can, because a firewall only logs addresses that actually connected to it.

That answer is used two ways: as evidence on the incident, and as a veto on the border blocklist, where an address the border never saw is at best an inert entry and at worst a shared egress whose blocking removes every legitimate client behind it. It is never used to lower a score: an attack behind a CDN is still an attack. The border lookup only reads; SATOM never writes to the FortiAnalyzer or the FortiGate — the firewall reads the published feed.
